plan:
FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN DOCUMENT
=================================

TITLE
Embedded chemical feedback (p-logP, QED, binding affinity) in a SMILES generator for targeted molecule discovery: a controlled comparison of in-generation feedback vs. post-hoc oracle selection vs. no signal.

1. RATIONALE

Brief claim (restated): incorporating a chemical feedback mechanism that leverages p-logP, QED, and binding affinity during generation (a) improves the production of molecules with superior chemical properties, (b) reduces molecular hallucinations, and (c) aligns generation better with real-world distributions, preserving structural diversity (e.g., avoiding over-representation of ultra-long carbon chains).

The design must test whether "embedding" the signal in the generator, rather than merely using the signal to select among outputs, is what delivers these effects. Three effects must therefore be separated: (i) no property signal at all (Baseline), (ii) the same property signal applied AFTER generation (post-hoc selection — a "score-using but not feedback-embedding" control), and (iii) the same property signal fed INTO generation (the treatment "chemical feedback loop"). Because the exact same property functions and oracle feed arms (ii) and (iii), any observed difference between them is attributable to the timing/mechanism of signal injection, not to which signal is used. This is the core contrast that answers the brief.

1.1 Environment truth (inspection result). The design is executed in a workspace that is empty (only task.json exists; track.md states "repositories and compute are not required"). Runtime: Python 3.14.4, no RDKit/torch/pandas/numpy, no network, no GPU, 224 CPU cores. Therefore all code, data, and oracles below are EXTERNAL DEPENDENCIES to be provisioned before the run, and every choice is a documented assumption. No results are claimed anywhere in this document.

2. ARMS AND THE MANIPULATED VARIABLE

One shared backbone: a character-level SMILES transformer (3 layers, d_model 192, 4 heads, dropout 0.1, ~1–2 M parameters), tokenizer = SMILES-level vocabulary (~80 tokens), trained with AdamW (LR 3e-4, cosine decay, wd 1e-4), batch 64, 30 epochs. Same architecture, tokenizer, parameter-init seed, data order, and hyper-parameters in every arm.

Arm A — Baseline (no signal). Backbone fine-tuned on the training corpus; generation at temperature T=0.9 with no property signal at generation or selection.

Arm B — Post-hoc oracle selection (signal AFTER generation; control). The SAME trained Arm-A generator samples candidates; from each seed's output pool, best-of-K selection (K=20) by the frozen oracle score keeps the K-top-scoring molecules. No in-generation feedback; the model itself is identical to Arm A.

Arm C — Embedded chemical feedback (treatment). The SAME backbone is fine-tuned with an in-generation feedback mechanism: on-policy policy-gradient RL, REINVENT-style, reward r(m) = sum_k w_k * f_k(m) + lambda_KL * KL(agent || prior) evaluated during decoding at every sampled token, back-propagated into the generator. This is the operationalization of "chemical feedback loop."

Arm D — Mechanism control (optional, budget-gated). Same feedback mechanism as C but with ALL property reward weights w_k = 0 (only the KL prior term remains). Detects whether any C-vs-B difference is an artifact of the RL procedure/stabilization rather than of the property signal itself. Retained in the core protocol because it is the same cost as one more C seed; if the CPU budget is exceeded it is the FIRST item dropped (it does not underpin the two primary contrasts C-vs-A and C-vs-B).

The manipulated variable across A/B/C/D is EXACTLY: whether and when the identical property signal enters generation. Nothing else changes.

3. CONTROLS (numbered, each mandatory unless stated)

Control 1 — Scoring-function identity (keystone). Arms B, C, and D consume the IDENTICAL frozen property functions and binding-affinity oracle: the same p-logP computation (same RDKit implementation), the same QED implementation, the same frozen surrogate affinity predictor, fed with the same input (canonical SMILES, same canonicalization), and the same normalization/scaling of all three signals (all three converted to [0,1] using a sigmoid/percentile mapping fitted ONCE on the training set). Arm A also evaluates with these same functions, but only for measurement, never for selection or generation. No arm may call a different scorer version or rescale the signals. This guarantees that any difference between B, C, and D is attributable to whether/when the signal enters generation.

Control 2 — Backbone and training identity. All arms share one architecture, one pretrained backbone, matched optimizer steps/epochs, batch order, and parameter-init seed; only the generation policy differs.

Control 3 — Timing control (selection vs. feedback). Arm B applies the same oracle as Arm C but after generation and without modifying the generator. C-vs-B is the central "embedding beats selection" contrast.

Control 4 — Matched sampling budget and seeds. All arms sample the same number of molecules per seed (50,000) at the same temperature (T=0.9; secondary exploratory T=0.7/1.0 without hypothesis tests) with matched RNG seeds per seed-index. Seeds: 5 for Arms A/B/C, 3 for Arm D. All arms get the same total sampling budget; Arm B additionally draws K=20 candidates per kept molecule (documented higher inference cost, not a training-budget change).

Control 5 — Stabilized RL reward. Arm C (and D) use REINVENT-style reward with a KL/prior-divergence term (lambda_KL = 1.0, clamped) against the pretrained baseline, preventing reward-hacking drift. No direct hallucination penalty is added to the reward, so hallucination reduction in C is measured as an EMERGENT outcome, not an incentivized one. (A documented variant adds an explicit out-of-support penalty; it is a sensitivity only, not a core arm.)

Control 6 — Property-reward ablation (Arm D). Isolates the property signal from the RL machinery (see Section 2).

4. TASKS, DATA, AND ORACLE

Targeted-discovery task (single primary task): generate molecules satisfying (i) p-logP in [0, 5], (ii) QED >= 0.6, and (iii) predicted binding affinity to one concrete target in the top-20% of the oracle's percentile ranking over the training set (assumption: dopamine-D2-type receptor target; a second target is documented but not run in the core protocol).

Corpus (assumption): a subset of a public SMILES corpus (MOSES/ZINC-clean): N_train = 120,000, N_val = 10,000, N_test = 20,000. Real-world reference distribution: an EXTERNAL held-out set (e.g., a 40,000-molecule ChEMBL-like sample) NOT seen in training; if the external set cannot be provisioned, the held-out test set substitutes and this substitution is recorded in the report.

Binding-affinity oracle (assumption, not structural docking): a frozen surrogate ML predictor trained on the chosen target's labeled affinity data (external dependency). Because it is a surrogate, reported affinity values are treated as ORDINAL (percentile/rank), never as true Kd. A SECOND independent oracle (different predictor/scoring method, frozen) is used ONLY for sensitivity S1 (hallucination-rate robustness); no arm is retrained on it.

5. HYPOTHESES → PRIMARY OUTCOMES

H1 (property improvement): In-generation feedback improves property scores.
- Primary outcomes: per-arm-seed means/medians of normalized p-logP, QED, and predicted-affinity percentile; targeted success rate = fraction of generated molecules passing (logP window AND QED cutoff AND affinity top-20%).
- Testable predictions: H1 predicts Arm C > Arm A (success rate, property medians) and Arm C >= Arm B on success rate with C's property values staying within the intended window (B may overshoot into extreme-but-invalid regions; see H2). Directional tests: C vs A and C vs B.

H2 (hallucination reduction): Feedback reduces molecular hallucinations. Hallucination rate H = H_invalid + H_out, reported SEPARATELY:
- H_invalid = fraction of generated SMILES that do not parse/validate under RDKit canonicalization.
- H_out = fraction of property-valid molecules (parseable AND passing the property filters) whose structural descriptors fall outside the empirical support of the real-world reference: longest linear carbon-chain length > 99th percentile of the reference, OR molecular weight outside [1st, 99th] percentile of the reference.
- Testable predictions: H2 predicts C < A and, critically, C < B on H_out (post-hoc best-of-K selection pushes B toward property extremes / out-of-support molecules, whereas in-generation feedback with the KL guard is expected to stay in-distribution). Directional tests: C vs A and C vs B, for H_invalid and H_out separately (no pooling across the two).

H3 (diversity and real-world alignment): Feedback preserves structural diversity and aligns generation with the real-world distribution.
- Primary outcomes: (i) internal diversity (mean pairwise 1 - Tanimoto over Morgan r=2/2048-bit fingerprints on valid unique molecules); (ii) Bemis-Murcko scaffold count and novel-scaffold fraction (scaffolds absent from the reference; if the exact scaffold set is rare, also report a scaffold-set overlap); (iii) distribution alignment: Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic and Jensen-Shannon distance between the generated and reference distributions over (a) longest linear carbon-chain length and (b) molecular weight; (iv) over-representation of ultra-long chains = tail mass of generated chain-length distribution beyond the reference 99th percentile.
- Testable predictions: H3 predicts C is closer to the reference (lower KS, lower JSD) than B on chain length and MW; C's internal diversity and scaffold count are not degraded relative to A beyond a pre-registered non-inferiority tolerance (e.g., diversity within 10% of A's, absolute). H3 also predicts Arm B (worst offender) over-represents ultra-long chains relative to C. The tension between H1 (push toward extreme properties) and H3 (stay in-distribution) is measured explicitly: per arm, report jointly the success rate and the out-of-support rate.

6. ANALYSIS PLAN

Unit of inference: per-seed aggregate metrics (n=5 seeds for A/B/C, n=3 for D). Because 50k molecules per seed are non-independent, per-seed aggregation is primary; pooled-molecule tests are secondary.

- Per-arm-per-seed: compute every metric (validity, uniqueness, novelty, diversity, scaffold count/novelty, property means/medians, success rate, H_invalid, H_out, KS, JSD, chain-length tail mass). Report mean ± SD (and 95% bootstrap CI) across seeds.
- Primary contrasts: (1) C vs A, (2) C vs B, for each hypothesis's primary outcome. Two-sided paired tests across seeds: paired t-test with Wilcoxon signed-rank as complement (n is small; report both). Secondary: Mann-Whitney U on pooled molecules for property medians; chi-square/Fisher on pooled counts for hallucination rates; two-sample KS (generated vs reference) with reported KS statistic and JSD as effect measures.
- Effect sizes: Cohen's d for property/success/hallucination metrics (with bootstrap CI); KS statistic and JSD as distribution-divergence effect sizes; non-inferiority criterion (10%) for H3 diversity.
- Multiple comparisons: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control across the metric family within each contrast; pre-registered, reported as adjusted p.
- Interpretation rule: H1/H2/H3 are SUPPORTED only if the relevant directional contrast is significant at FDR-adjusted p < 0.05 AND the effect size exceeds a pre-registered minimum (|d| >= 0.3); otherwise "no evidence of difference," not "evidence of no difference." C's hallucination reduction (H2) must be significant relative to BOTH A and B; otherwise the "reduces hallucinations" claim is only partially supported and this is stated.
- All generated molecules are saved (canonical SMILES + scores) so every sensitivity re-computation (including the second oracle) runs on the SAME saved outputs with no retraining.

7. FEASIBILITY (honestly bounded)

Concrete budgets (documented assumptions, CPU-only, 224 cores, no network at setup):
- Baseline fit: 30 epochs x 120k/64 steps ≈ 56k optimizer steps. Estimated wall-clock ~3–6 h (small transformer, CPU).
- Sampling (A, B): 50k molecules/seed/arm at T=0.9; ~1–2 h total for all A/B seeds.
- RL (C, and D): 5,000 on-policy updates, minibatch 64, with REINVENT-style KL stabilization; estimated ~1–3 h per seed-arm. Total estimated run ~40–80 CPU-hours across 5 seeds x (C + D) + A/B sampling. No GPU is used; if per-step throughput falls below 10 updates/s sustained, step counts are halved and the deviation is recorded.

Stabilization decision: REINVENT-style reward with lambda_KL = 1.0 clamp; if the KL term exceeds a pre-registered cap (KL > 3.0 nats on the eval set) OR reward plateaus for 500 consecutive updates, the KL weight is halved once (then RL continues); early stop at plateau +1,000 updates.

Pre-registered feasibility / abort criteria (no results are claimed; these gate reporting):
- AFTER Baseline: if validity on the fixed 5k eval sample < 20%, abort (data/model defect) and report the failure.
- DURING RL (each seed): if mean reward on the fixed eval set has not exceeded the initial baseline reward by update 3,000, the seed is marked "RL failed to train"; if >= 2 of 5 seeds fail, Arm C is reported as INFEASIBLE on this budget (a feasibility finding, not an effect) and no H1–H3 conclusion for C is drawn on its basis.
- Budget-forced drops (stated now): if the run exceeds budget, (1) Arm D is dropped first; (2) the full reward-weight grid sensitivity (S4) is dropped — only the single documented weight vector plus Arm D's zeroed condition remain; (3) Arm D seeds drop from 3 to 2.

8. FIXED-BY-ASSUMPTION PARAMETERS AND SENSITIVITIES (priority-ordered for CPU limits)

Assumptions table (each row = fixed choice; S = sensitivity; priority P1 highest):

| # | Parameter | Fixed value (assumption) | Sensitivity run (priority) |
|---|-----------|--------------------------|-----------------------------|
| A1 | Corpus & split | MOSES/ZINC-clean subset: 120k/10k/20k train/val/test; external ChEMBL-like 40k reference (fallback: test set, recorded) | S6: corpus size 300k (P6) |
| A2 | Generator | SMILES transformer 3x192, 4 heads, ~1–2M params, 30 epochs, batch 64, T=0.9 | S5: T=0.7 & 1.0 exploratory only, no tests (P5) |
| A3 | Task thresholds | p-logP in [0,5]; QED >= 0.6; affinity = top-20% oracle percentile | S2: window [1,4] and QED>=0.7, re-run metrics on saved outputs (P2) |
| A4 | Affinity oracle | Frozen surrogate ML predictor of chosen target; values ordinal (percentile) | S3: SECOND independent oracle re-scored over saved outputs, used for hallucination-rate robustness, no retraining (folded into S1) |
| A5 | Reward weights | w_pLogP=1.0, w_QED=1.0, w_affinity=1.0; lambda_KL=1.0; each signal normalized to [0,1] once on training set | S4: weight grid DROPPED for budget; replaced by Arm D zeroed-reward condition (P4) |
| A6 | Hallucination support | H_out defined via 99th-percentile support in chain length & MW | S1: re-compute H_out at 95th percentile AND with the second oracle — hallucination-rate robustness, no retraining (P1) |
| A7 | Seeds | 5 (A/B/C), 3 (D) | — |
| A8 | Stabilization | REINVENT KL/prior term, lambda_KL=1.0 clamped, early-stop rule | — |

Priority order (run if budget permits, in this order): S1 = hallucination operationalization robustness (95th vs 99th percentile; includes the second binding-affinity oracle per the brief); S2 = task-threshold sensitivity; S3 (second oracle) is executed as part of S1; S5 = temperature; S6 = corpus size; S4 = weight grid (dropped, see above). S1/S2/S3 all operate on SAVED outputs, so they cost only scoring time, which is why they rank first.

9. REPORTED OUTPUTS (deliverable contract)

A single self-contained report with: Rationale (this document's Section 1), Arms and Controls (2, 3), Tasks/Data/Oracle (4), Hypotheses->Outcomes (5), Analysis (6), Feasibility and abort log (7: recorded wall-clock, step counts, any aborted seeds with reasons), Assumptions table + sensitivities actually run (8), and a results table with all arms side by side (means ± SD/SE, FDR-adjusted p, effect sizes, CI) plus the generated SMILES/score archive hash. The report explicitly restates that H2 (hallucination) and H3 (alignment) are evaluated on property-valid molecules vs. the real-world reference and that absolute affinity values are ordinal. No experimental result is claimed in this design.

SCOPE OF THE DELIVERABLE
This document is the complete, self-contained experiment design. It is a design only; no code was written and no experiment was run. All empirical claims above are pre-registered predictions to be tested by a future execution under this protocol.
